faqs.question: What is the Zeiss SteREO Discovery V8 used for?
faqs.answer: It's a modular stereo microscope with an 8:1 manual zoom, used primarily in developmental biology and quality assurance, with configurable illumination for varied specimen types.

faqs.question: What does "modular" actually mean here?
faqs.answer: Focus, stage, and illumination are all chosen independently rather than fixed at purchase, manual or motorized focus, manual or motorized X-Y stages, and a choice of specialized illumination modules for different specimen and surface types.

faqs.question: What is the zoom ratio?
faqs.answer: 8:1, manual, with click-stops for discrete magnification steps that calibrate directly in ZEN imaging software.

faqs.question: Can the viewing angle be adjusted?
faqs.answer: Yes, the ergo phototube sets the viewing angle anywhere between 5° and 45°.

faqs.question: Is fluorescence imaging available?
faqs.answer: Yes, as an optional upgrade with PentaFluar S, supporting up to five different fluorescence filters.

faqs.question: What illumination options are available?
faqs.answer: Cold light (CL 1500 ECO fiber-optic, suited to living specimens) or LED (VisiLED), including a ring light combining brightfield and darkfield, and a Coaxial Reflected-Light Illuminator S built for specular surfaces.

faqs.question: Is this microscope suitable for polished metal or microelectronics inspection?
faqs.answer: Yes, the Coaxial Reflected-Light Illuminator S is specifically optimized for smooth, specular surfaces like polished metal parts and microelectronic devices.

faqs.question: Can a camera be attached?
faqs.answer: Yes, the 60N interface connects numerous phototubes for digital photo and video cameras.

faqs.question: How does this fit into Zeiss's broader stereo microscope range?
faqs.answer: SteREO Discovery V8 is the entry point into a documented four-model modular family, alongside SteREO Discovery V12, V20, and Axio Zoom.V16, all sharing compatible illumination, focus, and stage modules.

faqs.question: How is it different from Stemi 508?
faqs.answer: Both share an 8:1 zoom ratio, but Stemi 508 is built around apochromatic optical performance in a more fixed configuration, while SteREO Discovery V8 is built around modularity, specialized illumination options, and a direct upgrade path into V12 and V20.

faqs.question: Is there a return policy?
faqs.answer: Yes, a 60-day risk-free purchase. If it isn't the right fit, it can be returned with no questions asked.

faqs.question: Where can I find detailed technical specifications?
faqs.answer: Inkarp can request the full specification sheet from Zeiss.

faqs.question: What is the price of the SteREO Discovery V8 in India?
faqs.answer: Get in touch and Inkarp will put together a quote based on the illumination, focus, stage, and fluorescence modules selected.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of the SteREO Discovery V8 in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the Zeiss SteREO Discovery V8 in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

longForm.heroHook: One modular system. Five fluorescence filters. A viewing angle you actually choose.
longForm.heroLead: Most stereo microscopes lock you into whatever illumination shipped in the box. SteREO Discovery V8 is built the other way, an 8:1 manual zoom platform that fits directly into Zeiss's modular SteREO system, so the illumination, focus, stage, and fluorescence setup all get chosen to match the actual work, not the other way around. Click-stops lock discrete magnification steps, letting pixel sizes calibrate directly in ZEN imaging software. Choose manual or motorized focus, manual or motorized X-Y stages, and illumination built on cold light or LED, switching from shadow-free annular light to lateral oblique light at the press of a button. Add PentaFluar S for fluorescence, with up to five different filters. Add the Coaxial Reflected-Light Illuminator S for smooth, specular surfaces, polished metal parts, microelectronics, anything that scatters light unpredictably under standard illumination. An ergo phototube lets the viewing angle be set anywhere between 5° and 45°, so comfort stops being a fixed compromise. What it fits into: Zeiss's full modular SteREO system, alongside V12, V20, and Axio Zoom.V16. What it's built around: developmental biology and quality assurance, in equal measure. What it doesn't force: a fixed viewing angle, illumination method, or fluorescence setup.

sections.title: Illumination Built for the Surface
sections.tabSummary: What each specialized lighting module actually solves
body: Why every specimen type gets its own lighting module.

A flat, polished microelectronic part and a translucent zebrafish embryo need genuinely different light. One reflects almost everything back specularly, hiding detail under glare. The other needs gentle, uniform illumination that doesn't scatter or overheat the sample. SteREO Discovery V8 doesn't try to solve both with one fixed light source, it offers a module for each.

CL 1500 ECO fiber-optic cold light, paired with a wide range of light guides, is built specifically for developmental biology, gentle enough for zebrafish and Drosophila embryos without heat stress. The Coaxial Reflected-Light Illuminator S goes the opposite direction, purpose-built for smooth, specular surfaces like polished metal parts and microelectronic devices, with illumination and observation optimized specifically around the PlanApo S 1.0x objective. VisiLED ring light S 40-10 DF combines brightfield and darkfield in reflected light for PCB and surface inspection, and a light manager keeps coaxial lighting brightness stable through the entire zoom range, so illumination doesn't shift as magnification changes.

paragraphs: SteREO Discovery V8 isn't a standalone microscope, it's the entry point into a documented four-model family: V8, V12, V20, and Axio Zoom.V16, all sharing the same modular illumination, focus, and stage architecture. Zeiss's own product literature groups all four under one system profile specifically because accessories and modules move between them.

That matters practically, buying into the V8 configuration doesn't mean starting over if a research programme later needs V12's or V20's greater zoom range, much of the illumination and stage investment carries forward rather than being written off.

sections.title: eZoom, Explained
sections.tabSummary: Why electronic lens positioning beats a mechanical curve
body: Why electronic lens positioning beats a mechanical curve.

Every stereo microscope zoom body has to move lenses precisely as magnification changes. A mechanical zoom body does this with a physical cam curve, one fixed mechanical path that every unit follows, tolerances and all. Those tolerances compound as magnification increases, which is exactly where a soft image costs the most.

eZoom replaces that physical curve with stepping motors that position each lens electronically, correcting for the actual tolerance of the individual lenses in that specific microscope rather than assuming a uniform mechanical path fits every unit. Zeiss states the result directly: doubled precision compared to a mechanical zoom body, visibly more detail captured across the zoom range. The defocus curve stays tighter to the depth-of-field envelope throughout, rather than drifting outside it as magnification climbs.

paragraphs: Reaching away from the eyepiece to adjust magnification, focus, or brightness costs more than the second it takes, it breaks visual continuity with the specimen, and on a repeated inspection task that adds up across hundreds of samples a day.

SYCOP consolidates every essential function, magnification, focus, brightness, and current optical data display, into one control system operated by joystick and touchscreen, without needing to look away. Functions can also be assigned to physical buttons for operators who prefer tactile control, and the System Control Panel itself positions wherever the bench actually needs it, rather than being fixed in one spot regardless of how the workstation is laid out.

sections.tabSummary: Why 99% accuracy matters more than raw magnification
body: Why 99% accuracy matters more than the raw magnification number.

A 345x magnification figure is only useful if you can actually get back to it. Most zoom systems drift slightly every time they're adjusted, close enough for casual observation, not precise enough for a measurement or comparison that depends on consistent conditions.

eZoom solves that directly. User-defined zoom positions are set once and recalled with more than 99% reproducibility, which means a measurement taken today at a specific magnification and a measurement taken next month at the same defined position are genuinely comparable, not approximately similar. That reproducibility comes from the same electronic lens positioning that gives eZoom its 2x precision advantage over a mechanical zoom body, stepping motors correcting for individual lens tolerance rather than following one fixed mechanical path.

paragraphs: Moving from a wide overview of a specimen or component to fine structural detail usually means switching optics, or switching microscopes entirely, each swap introducing a chance to lose the exact field of view or reference point that mattered a moment ago.

V20's demonstrated range covers that whole span on one stand: PCB components imaged at 7.5x for overview and 150x for fine detail, the same component, the same setup, just a different point on the same continuous zoom. A daisy flower structure resolved at 150x visual magnification, a stained mouse embryo at 94x, all without a single optics change between them.

cta.lead: 345x magnification, 1000 LP/mm resolution, and a zoom that returns to the exact same spot, over 99% of the time.
cta.subheading: Authorized distributor and service provider. Demonstration, installation, AMC, and genuine spare parts.

heroParagraphs: The widest range in the SteREO Discovery family, and the one built for the moments when "close enough" isn't good enough. A 20:1 zoom range takes you from the largest overview straight into the smallest detail, and eZoom lets you set user-defined zoom positions and return to them with more than 99% accuracy.

That precision isn't incidental, it's the whole reason to choose V20 over V8 or V12. Total magnification reaches up to 345x, resolution up to 1000 LP/mm, both figures that only mean something if the zoom actually lands exactly where it's set every time.

The same SYCOP touch panel and joystick from V12 carries over here, controlling magnification, focus, contrast, and brightness without ever looking away from the eyepiece. And like every SteREO Discovery model, it integrates into the same modular illumination and accessory system as V8 and V12, so nothing bought for a smaller model gets stranded on an upgrade.

What it delivers: the widest zoom range, the highest resolution, and reproducible positioning in the family. What it doesn't sacrifice: depth perception, even at the top of that range. What it plugs into: the exact same modular system as V8 and V12.
